summary: Test strength runs each bound test through its declared runner and reads that runner's report, so that TypeScript criteria get the proof JavaScript criteria get (RC-46): bound tests under tsx node:test, vitest and @playwright/test; symbol-level and file-level Code Nodes in .ts, .tsx and .vue files; what stays unreadable recorded per criterion as BLOCKED (stage-keeper ruling Q2 (a)).
approach: Build order (the discovery study, section (4)), one write hand at a time: 1 tsx node:test and .ts Code Nodes (the type-stripped view from node:module stripTypeScriptTypes in strip mode, rewrites spliced into the original .ts at the same offsets; the structural resolver's .ts suffixes and its .js to .ts step for NodeNext specifiers; the callRemoval call-site set widened to .ts; the source refusal rewritten into the per-criterion BLOCKED; the runners list in rcf/test-strength.json; the TAP reader); 2 vitest (kind, the JSON report reader, " > " title paths and describe-title prefixes, vi.mock read as a mock); 3 @playwright/test (kind, the JSON report reader, the -g form); 4 .vue first and .tsx as its sibling (a downstream report's finding 1): the SFC script view of <script> and <script setup>, then the JSX scanner blanking each element to a same-length expression, a scan failure unsupported and never a guess. Design (study 2.1 B and 2.2 M2): runners entries { files, kind, argv }, first match wins; kind sets the default argv and the report the verb reads (nodeTest the TAP reporter, vitest and playwright their JSON reporter), argv replaces the whole argv and carries its own reporter flag; no match falls to the legacy runner with today's exit-code rule, else kind nodeTest; the verb never infers a kind. A bound test absent from its runner's report is exit 2, never killed or survived; a bound file failing to load under a mutant counts as killed, marked loadError beside killedBy. The pointer stays <file>::<name>, <name> the leaf title, the title path with " > " between describe titles and test title, or a describe title matched as a prefix of the title path; a leaf naming two tests in one file is exit 2. A blocked criterion carries result blocked, reason TEST_STRENGTH_UNSUPPORTED and a detail naming the file and the construct; the summary line counts blocked criteria; a run with one exits 5. Tests pin the experimental strip API on the engine floor (package.json engines). No separation change (study 2.5 S1). FBS-240 builds after this spec.

src/cli/test-strength.js: the help documents the runners field of rcf/test-strength.json beside the legacy runner, the blocked result and exit 5 (builder)
Code Nodes for every criterion of this spec (builder)
The queue, coverage and phase-3-6 goldens this DEFINE moves, regenerated through their declared generators with Generated-By in the first BUILD commit (builder)
notes: Round D DEFINE, 2026-10-29 (test-author), the round's first hand; story US-19904 (AC-19904-1 to AC-19904-7) under REQ-199, and AC-19901-9, the successor of the retired AC-19901-8 (the stage-keeper's retire-and-succeed ruling). Stage-keeper ruling Q1 (a): a parked vitest or Playwright unit whose config cannot score at its head gets one DEFINE: commit adding runners and a fresh Review; the verb never infers a kind from argv. Stage-keeper ruling Q2 (a): 0.39.0 carries RC-47's per-criterion BLOCKED (TEST_STRENGTH_UNSUPPORTED in the record, named per criterion with the file and the reason; light Finalise refuses it like a fail) for what it still cannot read: a non-erasable TypeScript construct such as an enum, a failed JSX scan, a non-TypeScript file. Further stage-keeper rulings of 2026-10-29 for this DEFINE: a pointer may name a describe title, matched as a prefix of the report's title path (run when a leaf under it ran, failed when any leaf under it failed); an unreadable bound test file or symbol-level Code Node is BLOCKED per criterion and a whole-run exit 2 stays only for the audit's own inputs (rcf/test-strength.json, the entry point, a runners entry); a blocked criterion is recorded result blocked, reason TEST_STRENGTH_UNSUPPORTED, detail naming the file and the construct, with an exit code the verb does not use today (5); each kind's default argv carries the reporter the audit reads and an argv override carries its own; a file-level Code Node on a non-code file keeps fileBlank; tsx, vitest, @playwright/test, vue and @vitejs/plugin-vue are the fixture projects' own devDependencies (test/fixtures/rc-46/*/package.json and package-lock.json, installed by the tests with npm ci), never rcf-lite's, so packages/rcf-lite/package.json does not change in this round. A downstream report's findings: (1) .vue Code Nodes are common downstream (one tree holds 163, 59 file-level and 104 symbol-level) and no tree holds a .tsx Code Node, so shape 4 is .vue first and .tsx a cheap sibling; (5) the structural resolver has no .js to .ts step, so NodeNext ../src/x.js imports of .ts sources read as not the entry; (6) one criterion bound to both vitest and Playwright tests needs two runner argvs, settled by the per-file runners rule. Named here, not built here (item 7): Node 24, vitest and Playwright print no TAP by default, so rcf build base-suite reports "no TAP summary" without a reporter flag: a line in the consumer upgrade notes, and a candidate rcf build base-suite warning. Fixture dependency pins: tsx 4.23.15, vitest 5.0.5, @playwright/test 1.64.1, vue 3.5.44, @vitejs/plugin-vue 6.0.10 (the synthetic packs keep their own lockfiles: tsx 4.23.15 and typescript 6.0.3; vitest 5.0.2, @playwright/test 1.63.0 and typescript 7.0.2), each admitting Node 24.0.0; the reds were proved on Node v24.14.0 (CI floats to 24.x).
title: rcf audit test-strength: TypeScript test strength over tsx node:test, vitest and @playwright/test bound tests and .ts, .tsx and .vue Code Nodes
